books.section: The Deepening of Partisanship in the Twenty-first Century
Threat of Terrorism, Increase of Presidential Power, and Economic Crisis (2001-2016)

options.text: Both parties agreed on the size of government after 2008
options.misconception: The Tea Party protested big government, which shows disagreement, not agreement.

options.text: Opposition to a new president could quickly become a national movement
The Tea Party ended partisan division in Congress
options.misconception: Division deepened; the movement was itself a sign of it.

options.text: The Tea Party supported every policy of the Obama administration
options.misconception: The movement arose to protest the administration's policies.

rationales.A: The Tea Party protested big government. That protest shows disagreement about the size of government, not agreement.
rationales.B: Background: the Tea Party grew from protests against big government and Obama's policies into a force that shaped elections, including the Republican gains of 2010.
rationales.C: Partisan division deepened after 2008. A protest movement is a sign of division, not its end.
rationales.D: The Tea Party arose to protest the administration's policies, not to support them.
rationales.general:
1. Ask what the Tea Party was. The account calls it a vocal opposition movement that arose after Obama's election, protesting big government.
2. Background: within two years, that opposition helped drive major Democratic losses in the 2010 election.
3. That speed shows how fast opposition to a new president could organize into a national movement.
4. Agreement between the parties and an end to division both contradict what the account describes.
Remember: a protest movement that wins elections shows opposition organizing, not agreement.

stem: What does the rise of the Tea Party after 2008 best show about American politics in the twenty-first century?

stimulus.source_note: Secondary account paraphrased from the grounding books (Barron's Premium 2027 Ch. 11; 5 Steps 2024 Ch. 30-31; Princeton Review Ch. 13).
stimulus.text:
Paraphrase of a secondary account: The presidential election of 2000 was one of the closest in American history. The vote in Florida was nearly even, and after weeks of legal fights, the Supreme Court stopped a hand recount in Bush v. Gore, a five-to-four decision that gave the presidency to George W. Bush. Partisan division deepened after that.

After Barack Obama won the presidency in 2008, a vocal opposition movement called the Tea Party arose, protesting big government and the new administration's policies. In 2016, Donald Trump won the presidency by carrying the Electoral College while losing the national popular vote to Hillary Clinton, the second time that had happened since 2000. Trump campaigned on border security, including building a wall, and on trade deals he said hurt American workers. The House impeached Trump twice, in 2019 and 2021, and the Senate acquitted him both times.
